# SitRep UI — Agent Guide

Read this before editing anything under `ui/`.

SitRep is a crisis-management tool used by civil-protection organisations during live incidents.
This directory is the front-end: a React 19 SPA built with Vite, talking to a GraphQL API.

**Active migration:** the backend is moving from Hasura's autogenerated CRUD schema to a
hand-written Go/gqlgen API. `src/api/` is the anti-corruption layer that makes that swap possible.
See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the ACL design and `api/schema.graphql` at the repo root
for the target contract. Do not add new Apollo/Hasura coupling outside `src/api/`.

---

## Setup

Requirements: Node (repo root `.nvmrc` pins `lts/*`), Yarn 4.

The UI needs two things running before it is useful:

```bash
# 1. from the repo root — Postgres, Hasura, and Dex (OIDC)
docker compose up -d

# 2. from the repo root — the Go server (fronts Hasura, terminates OIDC, serves /version)
go run .

# 3. from ui/
yarn install          # CI uses --immutable; do not hand-edit yarn.lock
yarn start            # opens http://localhost:3000
```

Port map:

| Port   | Service                                     |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| 3000   | Vite dev server (this app)                  |
| 4180   | Go server — proxy target for the dev server |
| 8080   | Hasura GraphQL engine                       |
| 5432   | Postgres                                    |
| 5556/7 | Dex (OIDC provider)                         |

The dev server proxies `/v1/graphql`, `/oauth2`, and `/version` to `localhost:4180`
([vite.config.ts:200](vite.config.ts#L200)). Requests go through the **Go server**, not directly to
Hasura — that is where the session cookie is validated. Without step 2 you get auth redirects, not
data.

## Before every commit — mandatory gates

All four must pass. CI runs the same checks and will reject anything that fails.
Run them in this order; `fmt` changes files that the others then check.

```bash
yarn fmt && yarn lint && yarn typecheck && yarn test --run
```

| Command           | Tool   | Notes                                                       |
| ----------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `yarn fmt`        | oxfmt  | Double quotes, 100-col wrap. Config: `.oxfmtrc.jsonc`       |
| `yarn lint`       | oxlint | Config: `.oxlintrc.jsonc`. Includes the ACL import boundary |
| `yarn typecheck`  | tsc    | `--noEmit`, zero errors required                            |
| `yarn test --run` | vitest | Single pass, no watch                                       |

If you touched any GraphQL document or the schema, also run:

```bash
yarn codegen && yarn codegen:check && yarn codegen:next:check
```

**`src/gql/` is excluded from `oxfmt`** — generated files use codegen's own quote style and
formatting them makes `codegen:check` report stale output. Commit codegen output exactly as
generated; never edit it by hand.

### Commit messages

Conventional Commits, scoped by area:

```
feat(api): migrate journal aggregate to anti-corruption layer
fix(map): preserve rotated popup positioning
refactor(api): replace hand-written wire types with generated types
chore(fmt): exclude src/gql/** from oxfmt
```

Common scopes: `api`, `map`, `codegen`, `types`, `fmt`, `release`.

## Testing

```bash
yarn test                          # watch mode (development)
yarn test --run                    # single pass (CI)
yarn test --run src/api/incident   # a directory or single file
yarn test --coverage               # v8 provider → coverage/ (Cobertura XML)
```

Config is in [vitest.config.ts](vitest.config.ts) (merged onto `vite.config.ts`), not in the Vite
config itself. Environment is `jsdom`; `globals: true` so `describe`/`it`/`expect` need no import.
[src/setupTests.ts](src/setupTests.ts) wires up `@testing-library/jest-dom` matchers, per-test
cleanup, and resets `fast-check` global config.

Tests live beside their subject (`Foo.test.tsx` next to `Foo.tsx`). Three tiers exist:

- **Mapper tests** — wire literal in, domain object out. Pure, no mocking. These are the only
  Hasura-aware tests and are the first thing deleted at cutover.
- **Container tests** (`*.container.test.tsx`) — mock the `api` module with the helpers in
  `src/api/testing/results.ts` (`loadingResult`, `errorResult`, `readyResult`) to exercise
  loading/error/empty branches. Do not reach for `MockedProvider`; this repo deliberately avoids it.
- **Component tests** — normal Testing Library rendering.

Coverage is uneven by design of history, not intent: only `incident/` has `commands.test.tsx`.
The other three aggregates have mapper tests but no command tests.

### Path aliases

Defined in `tsconfig.json`, which is the single source of truth — Vite picks them up via
`resolve.tsconfigPaths: true` ([vite.config.ts:195](vite.config.ts#L195)), so adding an alias
requires editing only `tsconfig.json`:

| Alias          | Resolves to                | Notes                                 |
| -------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `api`          | `src/api/index.ts`         | The only entry point views may use    |
| `api/*`        | `src/api/*`                | Internal — use inside `src/api/` only |
| `types`        | `src/types/index.ts`       |                                       |
| `types/*`      | `src/types/*`              |                                       |
| `gql`          | `src/gql/graphql.ts`       | `src/api/` internals only             |
| `components`   | `src/components/index.tsx` |                                       |
| `components/*` | `src/components/*`         |                                       |
| `utils`        | `src/utils/index.ts`       |                                       |
| `utils/*`      | `src/utils/*`              |                                       |
| `views/*`      | `src/views/*`              |                                       |
| `assets/*`     | `src/assets/*`             |                                       |
| `cache`        | `src/api/cache.ts`         | Legacy; prefer `api`                  |
| `client`       | `src/api/client.ts`        | Legacy; prefer `api`                  |

## Domain concepts

### Incident

The top-level entity — a civil-protection event (fire, flood, exercise). It has a name, a location
(WGS-84 coordinate string), responding divisions, journals, and map layers. An incident is open,
closed, or soft-deleted. **Only a closed incident may be deleted**; violating that is currently a
silent no-op at the Hasura layer, which `useDeleteIncident` converts into a named
`INCIDENT_NOT_DELETABLE` error. Closing an incident cascades to close all its open journals.

### Journal

Belongs to an incident; the structured log for one operational period or command post. Contains
messages. A journal can be closed and **reopened** independently of its incident
(`useCloseJournal` / `useReopenJournal`).

### Message

A single communication entry in a journal: sender, receiver, medium (Radio, Phone, Email, Other),
timestamp, content, and optional sender/receiver location detail. Each carries a triage status
(`Pending`, `MoreInfo`, `Reset`, `Triaged`) and a priority (`Normal`, `High`).

`Message.number` is **not** stored — it is computed from list position in `views/journal/listUtils`.
It is therefore filter-dependent today.

**Triage** happens in [TriageModal.tsx](src/views/journal/TriageModal.tsx): review a message, set
priority, tag relevant divisions, mark it actioned. Saving triage does a delete-then-reinsert of the
division tags and **depends on Hasura's multi-root transactionality** — if the deletes commit and
the inserts fail, the message loses all its tags. This is a real constraint the Go replacement must
preserve.

### Map, layers, and features

Each incident has one or more named layers; each layer holds GeoJSON features drawn by operators.

Rendering is **MapLibre GL** via `react-map-gl`. Drawing is `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw`. Features are
symbolised with **BABS** (Bundesamt für Bevölkerungsschutz) sprites — the standard Swiss
civil-protection symbol set, loaded from `@f-eld-ch/babs-sprites`.
[EnrichedLayerFeatures.tsx](src/components/map/EnrichedLayerFeatures.tsx) merges stored GeoJSON
properties with the sprite catalogue to drive the symbol layer.

Draw flow:

1. `MapboxDraw` fires create/update/delete; [Map.tsx](src/views/map/Map.tsx) handles them in
   `onCreate` / `onUpdate` / `onDelete`.
2. Those call `useAddFeature` / `useModifyFeature` / `useDeleteFeature` from `api`.
3. New feature IDs are derived with **`uuidv3(drawId, uuidv3.URL)`**
   ([Map.tsx:381](src/views/map/Map.tsx#L381)) — deterministic, not random. Changing this breaks
   idempotency of re-sent creates.
4. `useLayersForIncident` polls every **2 seconds** to sync across clients.

### Measures and Resource — stubs

`views/measures/{immediateMeasures,requests,tasks}` and `views/resource` are **placeholders**.
Every file is 9–15 lines rendering a heading; `NewForm` returns `null`. They have no API
integration and no persistence. `TriageModal` imports `NewForm as TaskNew` from `measures/tasks`,
so the empty component is on-screen but does nothing. Do not describe these as working features.

## Anti-corruption layer

`src/api/` is the boundary between Apollo/Hasura and everything else. Full design in
[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). The short version:

```ts
import { useIncidents, useCreateIncident } from "api"; // correct
import { useQuery } from "@apollo/client"; // only legal inside src/api/
```

Each aggregate has the same internal shape:

| File            | Purpose                                                      |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `documents.ts`  | `TypedDocumentNode` operations, typed from `gql`             |
| `mapper.ts`     | Wire → domain conversion; every field explicit, no spreads   |
| `queries.ts`    | `useQuery` wrappers returning `QueryResult<T>`               |
| `commands.ts`   | `useMutation` wrappers returning `CommandHook<Args, Result>` |
| `invalidate.ts` | `afterXxxWrite(id)` refetch helpers                          |
| `index.ts`      | The aggregate's public re-exports                            |

Mapper parameter types are extracted inline from generated types
(`FetchIncidentsQuery["incidents"][0]`), not from hand-written wire interfaces — those were deleted.

**Enforcement:** the oxlint `no-restricted-imports` rule in `.oxlintrc.jsonc` bans `@apollo/client`
outside `src/api/`. It is currently severity `warn` with a documented allowlist of legacy violators.
The allowlist may shrink, never grow. Adding a new direct Apollo import in a view is a review
rejection even though the linter only warns.

## GraphQL codegen

| Command                   | Effect                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `yarn codegen`            | `hasura/schema/hasura.graphql` → `src/gql/`. Run after editing docs |
| `yarn codegen:check`      | CI gate: fails if `src/gql/` is stale                               |
| `yarn codegen:next`       | `api/schema.graphql` → `src/gql/next/`                              |
| `yarn codegen:next:check` | CI gate: validates `*.next.ts` documents against the future schema  |
| `yarn codegen:schema`     | Introspects a running Hasura to refresh the SDL snapshot            |

`codegen.next.ts` matches only `src/api/**/*.next.ts`. Current documents use Hasura vocabulary
(`byPk`, `_eq`, `uuid`, `affectedRows`) that does not exist in the future schema, so they must never
be included. As each aggregate is ported, add a `documents.next.ts` beside its `documents.ts` and
the check picks it up — a burn-down that starts at zero.

`yarn codegen:schema` needs `HASURA_GRAPHQL_ADMIN_SECRET` in the environment. It is read from
`process.env` — never hardcode a secret in `codegen.schema.ts`.

---

## Internationalisation

Four locales: `de` (fallback), `en`, `fr`, `it`. Each is a single
`src/i18n/locales/<lang>/translations.json`.

**Adding a user-facing string means editing all four files.** There is no fallback-to-key safety
net that will fail a build — a missing key renders as the raw key at runtime, so the gap is only
visible by looking. Language is detected from querystring → sessionStorage → localStorage →
navigator.

Domain enum **values** are translation keys, nested under a namespace matching the enum:
`triage.DONE`, `priority.HIGH`, `medium.RADIO`. Lookups use an array fallback, e.g.
``t([`triage.${message.triageId}`, `triage.${TriageStatus.Pending}`])``
([Message.tsx:141](src/views/journal/Message.tsx#L141)) — so an unknown value degrades to the
default rather than rendering a raw key. Renaming an enum member means renaming that key in all
four locale files.

---

## Gotchas

- **Do not remove the `isEqual` guard** in `LayerFetcher`
  ([Map.tsx:192](src/views/map/Map.tsx#L192)). The layer query polls every 2s; without the deep
  compare, every tick dispatches new state and the map redraws continuously.
- **Polling is on by default everywhere**: layers 2s, incidents/journals/messages 10s. If you add a
  query, decide deliberately.
- **`refetchQueries` matches on document _and_ variables.** A refetch registered without the
  original variables silently never fires. Use the `afterXxxWrite` helpers in `invalidate.ts`
  rather than hand-writing `refetchQueries`.
- **Timestamps arrive as ISO strings, not `Date`.** Codegen types `timestamptz` output as `string`
  precisely so the compiler enforces this. Parsing happens in the mapper (`toDate` /
  `toOptionalDate`). Never assume a `Date` on a value that has not been through a mapper.
- **Generated nullability is accurate and often surprising.** Hasura marks many fields nullable that
  the old hand-written types claimed were required. Coerce in the mapper (`?? ""`), do not cast.
- **`src/gql/` must not be formatted.** If `yarn fmt` ever touches it, the `ignorePatterns` entry in
  `.oxfmtrc.jsonc` has regressed.
